subject.title: Feature Request: Cron Job Hooks System

question: Should OpenClaw core expose persisted per-cron lifecycle hooks that can run shell or webhook actions, and what trust boundary/API should own that behavior?
rationale: The remaining work changes public cron schema and can execute unattended commands or network calls, which requires product and security intent rather than a mechanical fix.

options.title: Design a core hook API
options.body: Approve a narrow, additive core cron hook/gate contract with secops-reviewed command/webhook permissions, runtime phases, failure semantics, and upgrade-safe docs/tests.

options.title: Keep hooks external
options.body: Declare that command cron plus plugin hooks are the supported path, and document the plugin/ClawHub pattern instead of adding CronJob.hooks to core.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Leave this issue open as an acknowledged product gap until maintainers are ready to own the security model and public API surface.

recommendation.title: Design a core hook API
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow, additive core cron hook/gate contract with secops-reviewed command/webhook permissions, runtime phases, failure semantics, and upgrade-safe docs/tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior review and current history make steipete the best available routing owner for the cron schema/runtime and product-boundary decision.
